item.title: Should I Invest in Bitcoin? – I Am No Longer a Bitcoin Maxi, Here Is Why (Bit coin, investing and wealth)
item.description:
After five years of putting every spare pound into Bitcoin, I explain why I am no longer a Bitcoin maxi and why going all in is a trap for most people. I also cover the bank that shut in Paraguay, the Chase outage and the hacked supermarket fridges, and why I still believe in decentralised money.




Want to talk through your own Bitcoin situation with an bitcoin OG, from buying your first to setting it up securely? Click here to send me a >>Whats app<<  


Or Email me at mylesdhillon@gmail.com 


Hit follow, so you never miss the latest insights on money, finance, investing and build wealth - plus clear guidance on cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, and Bit Coin for today’s serious investors.

item.title: Bitcoin & Beyond | Der New-Finance-Podcast – Der Krypto-König der Steuerfahnder | Anthropic und Co.: Chance oder Gefahr?
item.description:
Podcast Bitcoin & Beyond

Mancher Kryptoanleger denkt: „Ach, ich zahle keine Steuern – das Finanzamt bekommt mich sowieso nicht. Ist eh alles anonym bei Bitcoin und Co.“ Das könnte sich als folgenschwerer Trugschluss erweisen, wie wir im ersten Teil des Podcasts zeigen.

Wir haben mit dem deutschen Steuerfahnder gesprochen, der sich am besten mit Kryptowährungen auskennt: Er hat mit uns über seine Fälle gesprochen, erklärt, wie er Jagd auf Krypto-Steuersünder macht – und wieso die Luft für sie jetzt dünner wird.

Anthropic ist in aller Munde: Im zweiten Teil streiten wir darüber, ob es Anlegern nützt, dass sie neuerdings bei Börsengängen von US-Unternehmen wie dem des KI-Konzerns mitmachen können. Philipp ist begeistert, sieht Chancen und Geschichtsbuch-Momente – Lukas ein reelles Risiko, dass Anleger Geld verbrennen. Wer überzeugt Euch?

Link zum vollständigen Interview mit dem Krypto-Fahnder: https://shorturl.at/Vzr2r .

item.title: Rob Wallace | Bitcoin News – Can Bitcoin Survive? SoV vs. MoE Debate | Kyle Huber and John McCabe
item.description:

They break down the merchant’s-eye view of Bitcoin adoption, why Bitcoiners are one of the most valuable customer segments a business can win, what Steak ‘n Shake got right that almost every other merchant gets wrong, and what everyday Bitcoiners can actually do to speed adoption up. The path between zero and a million runs straight through real-world usage.

item.title: The Wolf Of All Streets – The Daily Wolf | Crypto beat Wall Street to the Anthropic IPO
item.description:
From The Daily Wolf with Scott Melker, live weekdays at 12pm ET on Yahoo Finance.

Anthropic prices its IPO tonight and lists on the Nasdaq tomorrow, and crypto traders have been trading it for days. Hyperliquid has a pre-IPO market, a $500 million subscription on Binance filled in about four hours, and Kraken and Ondo have their own versions. Scott Melker's point is that none of these give you the share, only the price.

The World Bank will explore paying development funds in USDC with Circle and Citi. Coinbase extended crypto-backed loans to all fifty states. And its AI stopped $4.7 million heading to a deepfake Elon Musk.

Timestamps
0:00 Crypto is already trading Anthropic before it lists
1:49 The offering terms, and where the pre-IPO markets are pricing it
3:02 Every way crypto is selling Anthropic exposure, and what you actually get
4:35 Bullish beats its revenue forecast as spot volume falls
5:46 Circle lets institutions mint and redeem USDC through DBS
7:12 The World Bank will study paying development funds in USDC
8:48 Coinbase extends crypto-backed loans to all fifty states
10:55 Waller wants a half-point hike, and what that does to the carry trade
11:57 Coinbase's AI stops $4.7 million going to a deepfake Elon Musk
13:17 Tampered Ledger wallets turn up in a Dubai Virgin Megastore

#Anthropic #Bitcoin #Crypto #Coinbase #USDC #DailyWolf #YahooFinance

item.title: The Pomp Podcast – BlackRock’s Bitcoin Bet Is Just Getting Started | Robbie Mitchnick
item.description:
Robbie Mitchnick is the Global Head of Digital Assets at BlackRock. In this conversation, we break down the lessons from IBIT’s record-breaking launch, why holders are converting their bitcoin into the ETF, and how fears about debt and deficits, plus bitcoin’s decoupling from AI stocks, are shaping the case for owning it. We also discuss bitcoin income products, staking, tokenization, and the regulatory outlook.

item.title: Bitcoin Today Recast – Bitcoin’s Longest Bear Market Ever? 13.4 Months and Counting | Nov. 18, 2026
item.description:
Bitcoin’s current bear market has reached 13.4 months. Could this become the longest Bitcoin bear market in history? Despite the drawdown, Bitcoin’s 200-week moving average has never recorded a down week in 650 weeks, and the long-term outlook still includes the possibility of a 100% return.

The discussion explores Bitcoin’s price decline, market cycles, and correlation with the Nasdaq, along with the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy and why Bitcoin’s network security sets it apart. The conversation also examines the AI boom, whether semiconductor chips or AI models hold the real competitive advantage, and what these trends mean for markets.

The episode closes with a perspective from Bitcoin Beach, where the focus isn't on Bitcoin’s daily price but on adoption, real-world utility, and how Bitcoin is changing lives.

item.title: The Bitcoin Layer – A Liquidity Crunch Is Breaking Every Market
item.description: In this episode, Nik walks through how widespread the breakdown in markets has become. Bitcoin lost its 200 day moving average and a trend line he has tracked since 2023, but it is not alone: gold is down $1,800 from its high, the S&P has closed below its 200 day, high yield bonds sit at their lows of the year, and oil and the broader commodity index have lost their uptrends. Nik explains why the dollar near its highest level since Liberation Day is the common thread, and why bitcoin tends to suffer most in tight liquidity and do best once policymakers inject it.

item.title: Bitcoin And | Bitcoin & Economic News – Astral Death Monster | Bitcoin News
item.description:
Bitcoin news and financial news update. Today I cover a German court's proposal to settle the Movie2k case for 40,000 bitcoin, South Korea's plans to let roughly 3,500 companies invest in Bitcoin, and the World Bank's partnership with Citi and Circle to test stablecoin payments. I also look at Polymarket's expansion into oil and natural gas trading, early criticism of OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra model, and Nvidia's decision to move forward without Jensen Huang.
Today's stories cover bitcoin regulation, institutional adoption, prediction markets, and the growing influence of AI on financial markets.

item.title: The Peter McCormack Show – #231 - Marcus du Sautoy - ⁠⁠AI Can See What Human's Can’t
item.description:
Marcus du Sautoy is the Simonyi Professor for the Public Understanding of Science at Oxford, a post he took over from Richard Dawkins and the author of The Music of the Primes, The Creativity Code, What We Cannot Know and Blueprints. For forty years he has been trying to resolve a single conjecture his PhD supervisor gave him. A few weeks ago, working with AI, he finally did and proved his supervisor wrong.


Marcus and I get into what that moment felt like, why prime numbers are the atoms of arithmetic and still have no pattern, the music hidden behind them, and why Marcus believes the universe is not described by mathematics but built from it. Plus the Russian who turned down a million dollars, Fermat's margin, and the physics behind Roberto Carlos's free kick.

item.title: Bitcoin News Alerts | Daily BTC Macro Signal – 2521: Bitcoin BEAR TRAP - JPMorgan's $266,000 BTC Target Defies the Market Crash
item.description:
Bitcoin is getting hammered, but JPMorgan's $266,000 BTC valuation is challenging the bears! With gold commanding an estimated $30 TRILLION market cap, Bitcoin reaching gold market-cap parity would imply approximately $1.43 MILLION per coin. Is this the ultimate Bitcoin bear trap?

Meanwhile, new research from River estimates that ten major financial firms increased their combined Bitcoin ETF exposure by approximately 54,400 BTC during Q3. Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, Bank of America, and even JPMorgan appear in the data. We break down the institutional money trail, the gold valuation math, and what this market crash could mean for Bitcoin's long-term future.

item.title: What Bitcoin Did – How Bitcoin Turns Trash Into Digital Gold | Daniel Batten
item.description:
“We looked at all the other solutions and Bitcoin mining was the only one that made sense.”

Daniel Batten joins me to explain how Bitcoin mining can make cleaning up pollution profitable. With his first landfill project in Mexico moving forward, we get into how capturing methane can turn an environmental problem into cheap power, Bitcoin and a new source of income.

We discuss the economics of one cent electricity, the upfront costs of getting these sites running, and why carbon credits are essential to making the model work. We also explore why these projects suit Bitcoin mining better than AI data centres, how they could decentralise the network, and what it would take to make Bitcoin carbon negative.

We finish with Greenpeace’s campaign against Bitcoin, Troy Cross’s conversations with the artist behind the Skull of Satoshi, and how Bitcoiners challenged the environmental narrative.

item.title: Dein Weg zu Bitcoin – Vom Bezirksdirektor der Bausparkasse zum Bitcoiner – warum Markus das alte Finanzsystem aufgab
item.description: Manche Gespräche laufen nicht nach Plan – und genau das macht sie wertvoll. 🙏 Ich hatte meine Fragen vorbereitet … und habe sie nach wenigen Minuten über Bord geworfen. Weil Markus so viel mitbringt, dass ich das Gespräch einfach fließen lassen wollte.Markus Vorsmann ist bei BitBox im Business Development und Mitgründer von BitUcation. Bevor er zu Bitcoin kam, war er über ein Jahrzehnt im klassischen Finanzsystem unterwegs – vom Azubi bei einer Volksbank bis zum Bezirksdirektor einer Bausparkasse mit großem Team.Was passiert, wenn du merkst, dass das System, das du jahrelang mit voller Überzeugung vertreten hast, nicht mehr deiner Wahrheit entspricht?👉 Warum die Eigenschaften von Bitcoin nur dann wirklich greifen, wenn du deine Bitcoin selbst verwahrst👉 Warum ein Fonds mit Versicherung oft komplexer ist als Bitcoin – und trotzdem kaum jemand nachfragt👉 Welche Geld-Glaubenssätze Markus aufgelöst hat und warum Geld für ihn heute Freiheit und Energie ist👉 Das Kontenmodell: wie du automatisiert Vermögen aufbaust – ohne Verzicht👉 Wie ein Podcast von Christian Bischoff den zweiten Anlauf zu Bitcoin ausgelöst hat👉 Warum Markus das alte Finanzsystem aufgab – und welche kleine Existenzkrise davor kamFür mich ist diese Folge der Beweis dafür, dass Bitcoin weit mehr ist als Geld. Wer sich ehrlich damit beschäftigt, beschäftigt sich irgendwann auch mit sich selbst: mit Verantwortung, mit Glaubenssätzen, mit der Frage, wofür wir eigentlich arbeiten.💬 „Ich kann von jedem etwas lernen – in jedem Gespräch.“ – Markus🧭 Genau um diese Fragen geht es auch bei FinanzBewusst: Geld wirklich verstehen – und für mich führt dieser Weg zu Bitcoin. item.title: Unchained – The Chopping Block: Crypto's Brutal Week With FalconX's Josh Lim, CZ vs. Star, the Anthropic IPO, and Should Jensen Huang Come Back?
item.description:
Welcome to The Chopping Block, where crypto insiders Haseeb Qureshi, Tom Schmidt, Tarun Chitra, and Robert Leshner chop it up about the latest in crypto. This week they are joined by Joshua Lim, Global Co-Head of Markets at FalconX.

Six red weeks in a row, BTC down to 65K, the fear and greed index at 10, and a $20 billion contraction in stablecoins. Josh walks through what his desk saw: a hidden buildup in leverage, end-of-year hedges in IBIT puts, and a weekend sell-off concentrated on Coinbase. The hosts react to the Situational Awareness 13F coming out down 92%, and Haseeb calls it the Multicoin of AI. Josh says the numbers don't support Star's claim that Binance is dumping on the market, and Haseeb explains how far back the CZ and Star feud goes. Then the Anthropic IPO: Tarun asks whether a flop would actually be better for crypto, Haseeb bets newly liquid Anthropic employees buy crypto, and Robert says Anthropic's unlock schedules are bringing the weirdness back. Tom asks what crypto's next catalyst is, and Haseeb and Tarun argue over whether past bear markets ever had a narrative. They close on Jensen Huang's exit from NVIDIA: Robert says he crossed a major line, Tarun makes the case that he willed NVIDIA into existence, and Haseeb says tech is misreading the moment.


Listen to the episode on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pods, Fountain, Podcast Addict, Pocket Casts, Amazon Music, or on your favorite podcast platform.


Show highlights

🔹 Six red weeks, BTC at 65K, $2 billion liquidated, and the fear and greed index at 10. Josh: it makes me wanna quit crypto. Haseeb: you can't open with that.

🔹 Josh on the hidden buildup in leverage, end-of-year hedges, and up to $40 million of premium spent on IBIT puts.

🔹 Josh won't name the DAT that's been selling. Tom names Strategy. Tarun: not delisted, removed from indices.

🔹 The Situational Awareness 13F comes out down 92%, and Haseeb calls it the Multicoin of AI.

🔹 Tom says the real signal is apathy: so many voices have left the room. Haseeb: that's the worst kind of capitulation.

🔹 Star says Binance is dumping. Josh says the net was to buy, and the selling is North Korea swapping back to ETH.

🔹 Haseeb on how far back the CZ and Star feud goes, and why HYPE is the most reflexive asset out there.

🔹 Josh expects rate hikes, a one-month malaise, and a recovery closer to January or February.

🔹 Tarun asks whether a flop Anthropic IPO is better for crypto. Haseeb says Anthropic money is coming for crypto.

🔹 Robert says Anthropic's unlock schedules would look familiar to anyone in crypto.

🔹 Tom asks what crypto's next catalyst is. Haseeb says every bear market feels like the last one.

🔹 Jensen Huang's exit from NVIDIA: Robert says he crossed a major line and is anti Bring Back Jensen.

🔹 Tarun says Jensen willed NVIDIA into existence, and every replacement candidate is mid.

🔹 Haseeb: this is not like Sam Altman, and the tech people who want Jensen back are miscalibrated.

🔹 Tarun stands by his one-liner: mistakes were made in pants he controlled.


Hosts

⭐️Haseeb Qureshi, Managing Partner at Dragonfly

⭐️Tom Schmidt, General Partner at Dragonfly

⭐️Tarun Chitra, Managing Partner at Robot Ventures

⭐️Robert Leshner, Founder & CEO of Superstate

Guest

⭐️Joshua Lim, Global Co-Head of Markets at FalconX


Disclosures


Timestamps 

00:00 Intro

01:11 Crypto's Brutal Week

07:09 Who's Selling Bitcoin?

12:51 Situational Awareness -92%

15:58 CZ vs. Star

22:30 Anthropic IPO and Crypto

30:10 Is This Bear Different?

35:09 The Jensen Huang Affair

41:04 Bring Back Jensen?

Learn more about your ad choices. Visit megaphone.fm/adchoices

The hosts react to the Situational Awareness 13F coming out down 92%, and Haseeb calls it the Multicoin of AI. Josh says the numbers don't support Star's claim that Binance is dumping on the market, and Haseeb explains how far back the CZ and Star feud goes. Then the Anthropic IPO: Tarun asks whether a flop would actually be better for crypto, Haseeb bets newly liquid Anthropic employees buy crypto, and Robert says Anthropic's unlock schedules are bringing the weirdness back. Tom asks what crypto's next catalyst is, and Haseeb and Tarun argue over whether past bear markets ever had a narrative. They close on Jensen Huang's exit from NVIDIA: Robert says he crossed a major line, Tarun makes the case that he willed NVIDIA into existence, and Haseeb says tech is misreading the moment.


Listen to the episode on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Pods, Fountain, Podcast Addict, Pocket Casts, Amazon Music, or on your favorite podcast platform.


Show highlights

🔹 Six red weeks, BTC at 65K, $2 billion liquidated, and the fear and greed index at 10. Josh: it makes me wanna quit crypto. Haseeb: you can't open with that.

🔹 Josh on the hidden buildup in leverage, end-of-year hedges, and up to $40 million of premium spent on IBIT puts.

🔹 Josh won't name the DAT that's been selling. Tom names Strategy. Tarun: not delisted, removed from indices.

🔹 The Situational Awareness 13F comes out down 92%, and Haseeb calls it the Multicoin of AI.

🔹 Tom says the real signal is apathy: so many voices have left the room. Haseeb: that's the worst kind of capitulation.

🔹 Star says Binance is dumping. Josh says the net was to buy, and the selling is North Korea swapping back to ETH.

🔹 Haseeb on how far back the CZ and Star feud goes, and why HYPE is the most reflexive asset out there.

🔹 Josh expects rate hikes, a one-month malaise, and a recovery closer to January or February.

🔹 Tarun asks whether a flop Anthropic IPO is better for crypto. Haseeb says Anthropic money is coming for crypto.

🔹 Robert says Anthropic's unlock schedules would look familiar to anyone in crypto.

🔹 Tom asks what crypto's next catalyst is. Haseeb says every bear market feels like the last one.

🔹 Jensen Huang's exit from NVIDIA: Robert says he crossed a major line and is anti Bring Back Jensen.

🔹 Tarun says Jensen willed NVIDIA into existence, and every replacement candidate is mid.

🔹 Haseeb: this is not like Sam Altman, and the tech people who want Jensen back are miscalibrated.

🔹 Tarun stands by his one-liner: mistakes were made in pants he controlled.

item.title: Bitcoin.com News Interviews – Why a $6B Crypto Hack Barely Shocks Wall Street | Animoca Brands’ Robby Yung
item.description:
Robby Yung, CEO of Investments at Animoca Brands, joins David Sencil at AIBC World in Rome. Asked whether the recent spate of hacks will blow crypto's reputation with people outside the industry, he says a $6 billion incident that is resolved in 24 hours just becomes a rounding error and that, after a financial-services conference in London, TradFi barely discussed last week's hack.

From there the conversation turns to agentic commerce, why he thinks AI agents need a public ledger to earn trust, and a broadband-era view of blockchain he credits to Lily Liu at Solana: eventually, people won't care that a transaction is on a blockchain. They'll just care that it works.

We cover:

  • How he says last week's hack landed in TradFi rooms
  • Muse, Instinct, and Animoca Minds as everyday agent platforms
  • His account of a Visa Hong Kong pilot, and the 30% U.S. e-commerce estimate he cites
  • Dynamic pricing, audit trails, and why Visa or Mastercard alone may not be enough for agents
  • The Lily Liu broadband analogy
  • UK property law for digital assets, Hong Kong dollar stablecoins, and tokenized stocks

Filmed at AIBC World in Rome.
Host: David Sencil

item.title: BITCOIN & ALTCOINS – Bitcoin und Altcoins unter Druck: Wo liegen jetzt die Chancen?

Der Abwärtstrend bei Bitcoin und Altcoins belastet die Marktteilnehmer. Der gesamte Kursvorsprung seit dem Sommer ist dahin. item.title: Onramp Bitcoin Media – The Shakeout Before $1,000,000 Bitcoin
item.description:
Bitcoin slid to about $61,000 as Jensen Huang left Nvidia and Anthropic lined up a $1.4 trillion IPO. Michael makes the case that this is the greatest shakeout Bitcoin has ever seen, and that the people selling now may be left on the sidelines.


BOOK A CONSULTATION

Holding Bitcoin for decades raises two questions: who protects it, and how it reaches your family. Onramp answers both. Three institutions protect it, and no single one can lose it, move it, or use it. Inheritance built in. Insured through Lloyd's of London. Speak with our team to see if it fits.

👉 https://go.onrampbitcoin.com/consult-fs-pod


GET ON THE LIST

• Onramp: our research, event invites, and the week's Bitcoin news in one free email. https://go.onrampbitcoin.com/research-fs-pod

• Early Riders Insights: the best content in the ecosystem, weekly. https://www.earlyriders.com/research


ABOUT THIS EPISODE

Bitcoin bounced near $61,000, above its summer low near $58,000, after a week in which Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO and tech stocks sold off with him. Michael argues this could be the greatest shakeout Bitcoin has ever seen, Brian separates a broken narrative from fundamentals he calls unchanged, and Liam explains why investors who do not manage outside money can buy at extreme value while funds wait for a catalyst. The hosts also unpack David Friedberg's idea of a backdoor in AI chips, why export controls may backfire, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's comments on Nvidia, and Anthropic's IPO: 825 million shares at $70 to $78 under the ticker ANT. Plus the FAA's nationwide ground stop, 21 banks' $270 million stablecoin venture, Coinbase and PNC, Alta's $80 million raise, Securitize buying River One, and whether AI agents still need stablecoins.


CHAPTERS

00:00 - The FAA ground stop and a week of outages

03:50 - Why everyone thinks Bitcoin is cooked

06:39 - Bitcoin's narrative versus its fundamentals

08:56 - The FAA, hacks and a WhatsApp exploit

13:48 - Jensen Huang resigns: David Friedberg on Nvidia

15:54 - A backdoor in AI chips and the export control fallacy

25:39 - A forced slowdown in the AI race

30:49 - Bessent, Nvidia's CFO and the calls to bring Jensen back

34:10 - Anthropic's IPO: ANT at $70 to $78

41:47 - Are investors rotating out of Bitcoin for Anthropic?

47:40 - The greatest shakeout ever? Why the thesis hasn't changed

49:36 - Price-insensitive buyers, and this moment versus $16K

52:47 - Banks' $270M stablecoin, Coinbase and PNC, Alta, Securitize

57:08 - Do AI agents still need stablecoins? SaaS as MCP servers

01:00:54 - Austin this week


ABOUT THE SHOW

Final Settlement is a weekly show on capital markets, dealmaking, early-stage venture, Bitcoin applications, and protocol development, presented by Early Riders and Onramp Media with Michael Tanguma, Liam Nelson, and Brian Cubellis.

• Connect with Early Riders: https://www.earlyriders.com/contact

• Michael: https://x.com/MTanguma · Liam: https://x.com/Lnelson_21 · Brian: https://x.com/BackslashBTC

item.description:
„Not your keys, not your coins“: Technisch gehört ein Bitcoin dem, der den Private Key hält. Rechtlich ist das aber nur die halbe Wahrheit.In dieser Folge spreche ich mit Rechtsanwalt Phil Hamacher darüber, wem ein Bitcoin vor Gericht eigentlich gehört und wie das LG Bonn in einem speziellen Fall urteilte.

Wir klären die Unterschiede zwischen Eigentum und Besitz und beleuchten wie sich das bestehende (und anzuwendende) Recht auf Bitcoin übertragen lässt.Natürlich sprechen wir auch über den berühmten „Bootsunfall“: Was passiert, wenn jemand behauptet, die Bitcoin bzw. Keys sind verloren?

Phil erklärt, welche Auskunftspflichten und Zwangsmittel greifen und warum Bitcoin kein Versteck vor Gläubigern ist, bis hin zu strafrechtlichen Konsequenzen.

item.title: The Bitcoin Treasuries Podcast with Tim Kotzman – Coinbase Shut Down His Account. So He Built Cake Wallet | Vik Sharma
item.description:
Vik Sharma, Founder and CEO of Cake Wallet and Radar Chat, joins the show to discuss how a darknet market purchase from his Coinbase account got that account closed, and how learning about chain analysis and spotting Monero on that same market sent him down the privacy rabbit hole that led him to self-fund Cake Wallet, which now has over 2 million downloads. He talks about mining Bitcoin in 2013 after the steel industry ground to a halt, why Cake was first to ship silent payments, and why he thinks people who want Bitcoin exposure in the stock market may simply buy an ETF instead of a treasury company, though he can't write them off yet. Vik also explains the idea behind Radar Chat, a fork of Signal with Bitcoin Lightning payments built into the chat, why builders should put Bitcoin into apps people already use instead of forcing normies into crypto products, building the Hyperliquid app Arbiter with AI, and why AI agents paying in Bitcoin is a matter of time.


Disclaimer: NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE - For entertainment purposes only.


Today's episode is brought to you by www.cakewallet.com/install and www.quantifyfunds.com.


Tim Kotzman on X: https://x.com/TimKotzman

Vik Sharma on X: https://x.com/vikrantnyc

item.description:
Rune Østgård joins the Bitcoin Infinity Show to talk about his new book The Reality Game and why monetary freedom and competing currencies matter more than most Bitcoiners realize. Drawing on his three years inside the European Commission, Rune explains the free rider problem, the archetypes of Team Freedom and Team Power, and why generous tit for tat beats civil war in debates like the BIP-110 fork. He and Knut also argue over whether Bitcoin’s number go up is the ultimate freedom tool or a trap that quietly changes the people who get rich from it.

item.title: Einfach Bitcoin Podcast – Bitcoin Wallet erklärt: Was eine Wallet wirklich speichert
item.description:
---werbung---
Bitcoin GRATIS eBook
https://klick.short.gy/Bitcoin-eBook
---werbung---


❤️ Danke für deine Unterstützung!

Jede Folge kostet Zeit und Herzblut. Wenn dir der Podcast gefällt, freue ich mich über ein kleines Trinkgeld. Schon der Preis eines Kaffees macht einen Unterschied.

☕ Kaffee ausgeben: klick hier

Wer zum ersten Mal Bitcoin kauft, sieht in einer App einen Betrag und denkt verständlicherweise: Die Coins liegen jetzt in meiner Wallet. Dieses Bild ist praktisch, aber technisch ungenau. Bitcoin liegen nicht auf dem Smartphone, auf einem Hardware-Gerät oder bei einem Anbieter wie Münzen in einer Geldbörse. Sie sind als Einträge in der Blockchain verzeichnet. Eine Wallet verwaltet die Schlüssel, mit denen man diese Einträge kontrollieren kann. Dieser Unterschied entscheidet darüber, was Besitz bei Bitcoin tatsächlich bedeutet.

Eine Wallet verwaltet Schlüssel, keine Bitcoin-Münzen

Die Blockchain ist das Kassenbuch, die Wallet ist der Schlüsselbund

Die Bitcoin-Blockchain dokumentiert, welche Bitcoin-Ausgänge unter welchen Bedingungen ausgegeben werden dürfen. Eine Wallet erzeugt und verwaltet die kryptografischen Schlüssel, die diese Bedingungen erfüllen. Mit dem öffentlichen Teil entstehen Empfangsadressen. Mit dem geheimen Teil kann eine Transaktion signiert werden. Erst diese Signatur weist dem Netzwerk nach, dass die Person, die ausgeben möchte, dazu berechtigt ist. Die offizielle Bitcoin-Entwicklerdokumentation beschreibt Wallets deshalb im Kern als Programme oder Dateien, die private Schlüssel verwalten und Transaktionen ermöglichen. Die technische Referenz erklärt dieses Zusammenspiel ausführlich.

Das Bild vom Schlüsselbund hilft dabei, nicht in die falsche Richtung zu denken. Die Wallet transportiert keine Coins von Gerät zu Gerät. Sie gibt dir die Möglichkeit, über Bitcoin zu verfügen, die im öffentlichen Kassenbuch des Netzwerks verzeichnet sind. Verlierst du den Schlüssel, bleibt der Eintrag in der Blockchain bestehen. Der Zugriff darauf kann aber verloren gehen.

Empfangsadresse und privater Schlüssel haben gegensätzliche Aufgaben

Teilen darfst du nur die Adresse, niemals den geheimen Zugang

Eine Bitcoin-Adresse ist für den Empfang gedacht. Sie lässt sich mit einer Kontonummer vergleichen, allerdings erzeugen moderne Wallets in der Regel viele verschiedene Adressen. Sie darfst du weitergeben, damit dir jemand Bitcoin senden kann. Aus einer Adresse allein lassen sich keine Bitcoin ausgeben.

Der private Schlüssel erfüllt die entgegengesetzte Aufgabe. Er ist der geheime Nachweis der Verfügungsgewalt. Wer ihn besitzt, kann eine passende Transaktion signieren. Deshalb ist die entscheidende Regel nicht, auf welchem Gerät eine Wallet installiert ist, sondern wer den privaten Schlüssel kontrolliert. Ein Screenshot, eine Cloud-Sicherung oder eine Nachricht mit diesem Geheimnis kann ausreichen, um den Zugriff dauerhaft zu gefährden.

Eine Seed Phrase ist die Wiederherstellung deiner Wallet

Zwölf oder vierundzwanzig Wörter können den Zugang sichern

Viele moderne Wallets verwenden eine Seed Phrase, auch Wiederherstellungsphrase genannt. Diese Wortfolge dient als Grundlage, aus der eine Wallet die benötigten Schlüssel ableiten kann. Häufig besteht sie aus zwölf oder vierundzwanzig Wörtern. Der technische Standard BIP39 beschreibt genau dieses Prinzip: Eine leicht notierbare Wortfolge wird in einen Seed für deterministische Wallets umgewandelt. Die BIP39-Spezifikation dokumentiert den Aufbau.

Das erklärt, warum die Seed Phrase so sensibel ist. Wer sie kennt, braucht weder dein Telefon noch ein Hardware-Gerät, um eine kompatible Wallet wiederherzustellen. Umgekehrt kann sie den Zugang retten, wenn ein Gerät kaputtgeht, verloren geht oder ersetzt wird. Sie ist kein Passwort, das ein Anbieter auf Anfrage zurücksetzen kann, sondern der Schlüssel zu deiner eigenen Wiederherstellung.

Verwahrung bei einem Anbieter und Selbstverwahrung sind verschiedene Modelle

Komfort kann Verantwortung abnehmen, aber nicht die Frage des Eigentums ersetzen

Bei einer verwahrten Lösung führt ein Anbieter die technischen Schlüssel. In der App erscheint zwar dein Bestand, die eigentliche Schlüsselverwaltung liegt aber beim Dienstleister. Das kann den Einstieg vereinfachen: Zugangsdaten lassen sich häufig zurücksetzen, und der Anbieter übernimmt Teile der technischen Absicherung. Dafür bist du darauf angewiesen, dass der Dienst zuverlässig arbeitet und Auszahlungen ermöglicht.

Bei der Selbstverwahrung kontrollierst du die Wiederherstellungsinformationen selbst. Das schafft Unabhängigkeit, verlagert aber auch die Verantwortung. Ein verlorener Zugang lässt sich nicht über einen Kundenservice zurückholen. Die österreichische Finanzmarktaufsicht weist bei ihrer Information zur Krypto-Verwahrung auf genau diesen Zielkonflikt hin: Regulierte Anbieter können bestimmte organisatorische und technische Schutzmaßnahmen bieten, während private Schlüssel bei der Selbstverwahrung besonders sorgfältig geschützt werden müssen. Die FMA ordnet Wallets und Zugangsschlüssel ein.

Die passende Wallet richtet sich nach dem Zweck, nicht nach einem Werbeversprechen

Erst verstehen, dann über eine Lösung entscheiden

Eine Software-Wallet kann für kleine Beträge oder das Kennenlernen der Technik praktisch sein. Ein separates Hardware-Gerät kann Schlüssel so verwahren, dass sie nicht dauerhaft auf einem internetverbundenen Computer liegen. Beides ist nicht automatisch richtig oder falsch. Entscheidend sind der eigene Kenntnisstand, der geplante Nutzungszweck und die Bereitschaft, Verantwortung für Backups zu übernehmen.

Bevor du eine Wallet einrichtest oder Bitcoin dorthin sendest, lohnt sich ein ruhiger Test ohne Zeitdruck. Verstehe, wie du eine Empfangsadresse überprüfst, wie eine Wiederherstellung grundsätzlich funktioniert und welche Daten niemals weitergegeben werden dürfen. Bitcoin-Transaktionen lassen sich nach der Bestätigung in der Regel nicht zurückholen. Sicherheit beginnt deshalb nicht mit einem Produkt, sondern mit dem Verständnis, was die Wallet eigentlich schützt.

Zusammenfassung

Eine Bitcoin Wallet speichert nicht die Bitcoin selbst. Sie verwaltet die privaten Schlüssel oder Wiederherstellungsinformationen, mit denen sich Bitcoin in der Blockchain kontrollieren lassen. Eine Empfangsadresse darf geteilt werden, private Schlüssel und Seed Phrase niemals. Wer einen Anbieter nutzt, gibt die Schlüsselverwaltung teilweise ab; wer selbst verwahrt, gewinnt Kontrolle und übernimmt zugleich die volle Verantwortung. Dieses Grundwissen gehört vor jede Entscheidung über Kauf, Verwahrung oder Transfer.

Häufige Fragen zur Bitcoin Wallet

Liegen Bitcoin auf einer Hardware-Wallet?

Nein. Die Bitcoin bleiben als Einträge in der Blockchain. Eine Hardware-Wallet bewahrt in erster Linie die Schlüssel so auf, dass sie bei einer Transaktion möglichst nicht auf einem internetverbundenen Gerät offengelegt werden.

Kann jemand mit meiner Bitcoin-Adresse meine Bitcoin stehlen?

Nein. Die Adresse dient dem Empfang und darf weitergegeben werden. Zum Ausgeben benötigt man den zugehörigen privaten Schlüssel beziehungsweise die Wiederherstellungsinformationen.

Was passiert, wenn ich meine Seed Phrase verliere?

Wenn du zugleich keinen anderen funktionierenden Zugang mehr zur Wallet hast, kann der Zugriff dauerhaft verloren sein. Deshalb sollte die Phrase niemals leichtfertig gespeichert oder an Dritte weitergegeben werden.

Ist Selbstverwahrung automatisch besser?

Nicht für jede Person und jede Situation. Sie bietet mehr technische Kontrolle, verlangt aber auch, dass du deine Wiederherstellungsinformationen sicher verwahrst und die Folgen eines Fehlers selbst trägst. Das ist keine Anlageempfehlung.

item.title: Bitcoin, Fiat & Rock'n'Roll – Why Headline Stablecoin Volume Misleads: A BIS paper on Ethereum Transaction Data
item.description:
What on-chain data really tells us about stablecoin adoption, payment activity and the future of financial infrastructure.

Fabian explains why 31.6% of stablecoin-related transactions involve additional contract interactions, and why starting point changes the interpretation. They cover composability and atomicity, the limits of headline volume figures, skepticism about retail stablecoin payments and tokenized deposits, and a possible role for wholesale CBDC in institutional settlement. Fabian urges banks to study blockchain data directly.

Fabian Schär et al., The Anatomy of Stablecoin Transactions. BIS Working Paper 1359. Bank for International Settlements.

Allium State of Stablecoins and Payments Report Q3 2026, Oct 15 2026

Visa On-Chain Analytics

Recent BIS papers on Stablecoin Usage in Payments:

  • Aldasoro, I., Frost, J., & Ito, H. (2026). The Impact of Stablecoins on the International Monetary and Financial System. BIS Papers 170. Bank for International Settlements.
  • Du, W., Huang, C., & Scharfstein, D. (2026). Competing rails for crossborder payments: banks, fintechs, and stablecoins. BIS Working Paper 1385. Bank for International Settlements.

item.title: Bitcoin verstehen – Episode 340 - 5 Situationen, in denen du (noch) keine Bitcoin kaufen solltest
item.description:
🔐 Wir veranstalten Live-Masterclasses zur Bitcoin-Aufbewahrung: Von der Ersteinrichtung einer Hardwarewallet bis zu fortgeschrittenen Themen wie optionaler Passphrase und Multisig. Trag dich in die Warteliste ein und erfahre als Erstes, wann es losgeht.


In dieser Folge sprechen wir über fünf Situationen, in denen du (noch) keine Bitcoin kaufen solltest: kein Notgroschen, teure Schulden, ein zu kurzer Anlagehorizont, falsche Motive wie FOMO und Panik sowie eine ungeklärte Aufbewahrung und Nachlass. Dazu geht es um die Frage, welchen Betrag du bei einem starken Preisrückgang aushältst, und was du vor deinem ersten Kauf klären kannst.

item.title: House of Satoshi - Bitcoin und Friends – #69 Bitcoin Mining verstehen | Alex Arisi, Mitgründer Dezentralshop
item.description:
*** In eigener Sache: Unser Bitcoin AI Strategy ETP (BTCAI) ist an der SIX Swiss Exchange handelbar. Das Prinzip: Bitcoin, wenn's läuft. Cash, wenn's kracht. Alle Infos, Factsheet und Risiken: https://btcai.house-of-satoshi.ch

Werbung. Bitcoin-Investments sind mit erheblichen Risiken bis zum Totalverlust verbunden. ***


Alle zehn Minuten ein neuer Block, egal ob zehn oder zehn Millionen Rechner mitwürfeln. Wie schafft Bitcoin das, und was passiert, wenn grosse Miner ins KI-Geschäft wechseln?


Alex Arisi hat am Pizza Day 2022 den Dezentralshop mitgegründet. Mit Rino geht er das Mining von Grund auf durch, vom Kinderspiel bis zur Frage, wer Bitcoin überhaupt angreifen könnte.


Darum geht's

  • Mining für Zwölfjährige: Yazzi, aber mit einer Million Würfeln
  • Nodes sind die Polizisten, Miner die Arbeiter, und warum das früher dasselbe Gerät war
  • Schwer zu lösen, leicht zu prüfen: worauf die Sicherheit von Bitcoin beruht
  • Die Difficulty als eingebaute Intelligenz: warum es im Schnitt bei zehn Minuten bleibt, auch wenn ein Supercomputer dazukommt
  • Miner wechseln zur KI, BlackRock kauft Bitcoin: warum Alex beides nicht als Gefahr sieht und was er stattdessen fürchtet
  • Zum Schluss praktisch: wie du mit einer Bitaxe selber minen kannst


Weiterführende Links

  • Dezentralshop: https://dezentralshop.ch/
  • Hashrate live: https://www.blockchain.com/de/explorer/charts/hash-rate
  • Bitaxe: https://bitaxe.org/
  • Blitzpool (Solo-Mining-Pool aus der Schweiz): https://blitzpool.yourdevice.ch
  • Bitcoin-Miner und Tassenwärmer in einem https://dezentralshop.ch/product/meincoffee-gekkoscience-700-gh-s-kaffewaermer/

item.title: Bitcoin Audible – Does capitalism ruin everything? (Enshittification Q&A P1)
item.description:
In this episode, I walk through listener comments on the recent "The Enshittification of Everything" Guy's Take and what the endless cheapening of everything really means for our economy.

I discuss why many mistakenly blame free markets for corporate greed, the difference between real capitalism and fiat-driven monopolies, and how fake interest rates completely warp business incentives. I also share why sound money and natural deflation are the only ways to actually fix the broken products and services we deal with every single day.

(00:04:56) - The real price of products

(00:08:15) - The king of consumerism?

(00:09:23) - The control of capital

(00:11:30) - Private equity and other factors

(00:27:03) - Capitalism and money printing

item.title: Bitcoiners - Live From Bitcoin Beach – How El Salvador Is Making Bitcoin Self-Custody Work Without a Bank, Data or a Smartphone! | Darvin Otero of Tiankii
item.description:
What does it take for 120 families in El Zonte to pay their social housing loans in Bitcoin, or for a hotel on Cloudbeds to take it at booking?

You’ve heard El Salvador put Bitcoin in front of a whole country. What’s harder to see from outside is which tools people are actually using now.

Mike sat down with Darvin Otero of Tiankii, one of the first local Bitcoin builders in El Salvador and a Bitcoiner since before the Bitcoin Law.

Darvin’s team started with tap-to-pay cards for people with no smartphone or no data, back when El Salvador became the Lightning Network’s first nationwide test. For the last year and a half they’ve focused on self custody, and Darvin explains how a self custody wallet on Spark can collect payments while it’s offline.

That work feeds the Bitcoin Payment Hub, a pre-printed QR code payment stand that stays dormant until a merchant connects a wallet. Each code carries a short Lightning address that works from a feature phone, and one feature exists because of the cracked phone cameras Darvin kept seeing at checkout.

Most hotels in El Zonte run on Cloudbeds, where paying in Bitcoin used to mean messaging the front desk and waiting for someone to send a QR code. Card fees in the region run 5 to 8%. Tiankii now puts Bitcoin inside the booking itself.

In the housing project, each family’s loan is in dollars and paid in Bitcoin, and their QR code doubles as their loan number. Some families don’t earn Bitcoin yet, so they can pay cash at a K1 ATM. Darvin also describes what happens when a parent working far from home wants to cover the payment...

He’s proud of the Salvadoran talent coming out of Cubo Plus and the Bitcoin Office, and of new circular economies in Chalatenango and Suchitoto. He’d still like more places to pay, and he’s watching grants go everywhere except to Salvadoran developers.

These are Salvadorans building the tools their own neighbors pay with, bear market or bull market!

If you run a hotel, a shop or a dev team, listen to this one before you decide what Bitcoin can do in El Salvador.


—Bitcoin Beach Team

item.title: Nodesignal - Deine Bitcoin-Frequenz – Nodesignal-Talk - E302 - libbitcoin is coming
item.description:
In der heutigen Folge sprechen Jan-Paul und Thorsten mit Kevin (Eynhaender) über Libbitcoin, die zweite, von Grund auf neu gebaute Umsetzung des Bitcoin-Regelwerks neben Bitcoin Core. Wir klären, was Libbitcoin ist und wie es ohne eigenes UTXO-Set funktioniert. Außerdem geht es um Bitcoin-Node-Vielfalt, Performance, Electrum-Server und Block-Explorer als Teil des Baukastens.

item.title: Stephan Livera Podcast – Robert Warren: Do Mining Pools Actually Threaten Bitcoin? | SLP789
item.description:
Robert Warren, Head of Comms at Elektron Energy, says Bitcoin mining pools do centralize something, but it is mainly control of block templates, not the power to reorg the chain. He treats FPPS as an insurance product: pools take variance and charge a fee, and a miner who doesn't like the deal can switch to a fallback pool almost immediately.

Stephan and Rob also walk through AntPool white-labeling, why a run of Foundry or SpiderPool blocks is usually just variance, why listed miners are leasing sites to AI and HPC, and why Elektron is staying bitcoin-first. Rob argues network security barely changes as public hashrate rotates to private operators, and that hashrate is still going up and to the right.

item.title: The "What is Money?" Show – Bitcoin is Ending Real Estate's 50 Year Run w/Leon Wankum
item.description:
Leon Wankum joins Robert Breedlove to make the case that real estate and Bitcoin are complementary assets, and that Bitcoin is the one variable that never changes, in a monetary system where everything else does.

They cover why commercial real estate was the best performing asset class for fifty years and why that generational run is now reversing, how German tax law lets him sell property tax free after ten years and Bitcoin after one, why his peers get triggered by him and why that is a signal, the Tesla lesson for German real estate, and his call that Bitcoin will be the first quadrillion dollar asset while houses return to being a place to live.

item.title: Bitcoin Takeover Podcast – S17 E51: Martti Malmi on Iris, NostrVPN and Freedom Tech
item.description:
We recorded this at Bitcoin Amsterdam, the Bitcoin Magazine conference, with legendary cypherpunk and Satoshi contributor Martti Malmi. This is his second time on the show. Two years ago in Prague we talked about 2009, the forum, and the man who signed his emails Satoshi Nakamoto. This time I had promised we would talk about what he is building now. The conference still put him on a history panel.

Martti would rather talk about Iris, the Nostr client at iris.to, and especially NostrVPN, which he describes as Tailscale without the Tailscale company: your devices find each other on Nostr, with no email login and no coordination server. Underneath is FIPS, an ad-hoc mesh routing protocol. He also walks through Iris Chat, Iris Drive, git.iris.to, Hashtree, and a directory of about 20 apps at apps.iris.to. He is not making money from any of it, and he does not think software is a great business model anymore. Finnish people, he says, tend to be a bit ideological and not great businessmen. Maybe he is the same way.

We talk about Nostr in a bear market, about building for AI agents versus building for humans, and about permissionlessness as the reason an agent might pick Nostr at all. I put my usual heresy to him, that Bitcoin is now a family of projects, and he stays open-minded: if network effects dissolve, funds may gravitate to the best store of value and the best way to pay, and the biggest network may matter less. For him, Bitcoin is still mostly a store of value. He would like to tap to pay and not have to tell the merchant he wants to pay in Bitcoin.

We do break the "no Satoshi" rule twice. Martti is the one who set bitcoin.org up on WordPress, and he still thinks the man who struggled with that setup was "just a guy," unless you prefer the joke that the integer overflow bug was planted to make a time-travelling AI look human. And he remembers Satoshi paying him for the website work in US dollars, in an envelope, sent to his father's address so it would not sit on a dorm floor. He does not have the original envelope. His grandfather, in 2009, thought this could become a global reserve currency, and did not buy any. Years later, after another crash headline, his father messaged him: "I hope you sold early." And he did.

In between there is the year he stopped writing code himself, "meat agents" in smart glasses, a romantic argument that the best life extension technology is having kids, Michael Pollan on simulated feeling, and a fifty-percent kind of optimism about permissionless tech. You can find him on Nostr as Sirius, at iris.to/sirius. The name comes from the pun, the star, and Sirius Black.

What we cover:

  • Why history panels still haunt him, and why he wanted to shill the new work
  • NostrVPN as a peer-to-peer Tailscale alternative, and FIPS mesh routing
  • Iris Chat, Iris Drive, git.iris.to, Hashtree, and the apps.iris.to directory
  • Why he is not trying to make money from software
  • Nostr's chicken-and-egg problem, bots, and a bet on agentic use
  • Whether we are building for humans or for agents
  • Bitcoin as a family of projects, and dissolving network effects
  • Payments, Lightning, Square, BTCPay, and tap to pay
  • The bitcoin.org WordPress story, and "oh, he's just a guy"
  • The year he wrote no code, longevity, and consciousness
  • Satoshi, an envelope of dollars, and "I hope you sold early"
  • How to find him: Sirius, iris.to/sirius, and the three links to try first

This episode is sponsored by SideShift, Cake Wallet, eCash / LayerTwo Labs, Braiins Hashpower, and Orange Rock.

The previous conversation is S16 E12: Martti Malmi on Bitcoin in 2009 & Satoshi Nakamoto, at bitcoin-takeover.com/s16-e12-martti-malmi-on-bitcoin-in-2009-satoshi-nakamoto/. His published correspondence with Satoshi is at mmalmi.github.io/satoshi/. The full Bitcoin Takeover archive is at bitcoin-takeover.com.

item.title: Thank God for Bitcoin – TGFB Episode 84: AI and Anthropology with Jon Barlow
item.description:
Jonathan Barlow, Associate Director of Mississippi State University's Data Science Program, discusses the intersection of AI, anthropology, and technology, exploring what it means to be human in the age of AI. He reflects on his experiences with AI in education and job placement, the ethical implications of humanoid robots, and the economic factors influencing AI development. Barlow emphasizes the importance of understanding the unique aspects of human nature in relation to AI and cautions against the potential dangers of anthropomorphizing technology. The discussion also touches on the skepticism surrounding AI catastrophizing, the aesthetic critiques of technology, and the empowering potential of AI for households and ministries.

https://x.com/barlowjon?s=20

https://theopolisinstitute.com/search/?author=jon-barlow

  • Bitcoin Core security disclosure policy

Pull requests and discussion

  • Tor proof-of-work defenses: #33414
  • CJDNS support: discussion #36041 and release-note update #36202
  • Replacing libevent with a custom HTTP server: #35182
  • More inbound block-relay capacity: #28463
  • Fetching block inputs in parallel: #35295
  • Removing the experimental warning from send and sendall: #35601
  • Watch-only wallet exports: RPC #32489 and GUI #872

item.title: #NotAnotherBitcoinPodcast – #NotAnotherBitcoinPodcast: Bitcoin Cash Fork Day — The Live Countdown (Aug 1, 2017)
item.description: How goes it? Five straight hours live on the day Bitcoin Cash forked off Bitcoin — and Kenn is on air for all of it, with the Coindance countdown on screen and under two hours to go when the stream starts.This is a working session, not a recap. Kenn tries to get at his BCC on his Ledger live (the Ledger Blue suddenly offering four different Bitcoin chains to pick from is a moment in itself), walks the chat through exactly how to sweep a paper wallet and split BTC from BCC with the Jaxx tool, and puts BTC's price on the record while he works: $2,775 on Coinbase.He also calls out the fork scams in real time — including a paid Facebook ad telling people to send their Bitcoin to a stranger's address to "receive" their forked coins — and says the thing that still matters: don't trust somebody else with your private keys. Personal responsibility era. Oh, and somewhere in there he agrees to give away 0.1 BCC, because of course he does. One thing he won't do: open his wallet on camera. Not happening.Super chats, the regulars in the chat box, and a front-row seat to the biggest chain split crypto had ever seen, caught as it happened — not remembered, not rewritten. Live.How goes it? Have a day.

item.title: Allt om Bitcoin – #32 Bitcoins ketchupeffekt
item.description:
Kan AI-boomen ha bidragit till att Bitcoin steg mindre än många väntade sig efter halveringen? I avsnitt 32 undersöker jag hur AI-investeringar, billigare AI-modeller och frågetecken kring lönsamheten kan påverka vart kapitalet söker sig härnäst.

Samtidigt växer USA:s statsskuld och konkurrensen om köpare till amerikanska statsobligationer hårdnar. Jag går igenom hur förändrade kapitalflöden från Kina, Japan och Gulfstaterna kan påverka dollarn – och varför guld och Bitcoin kan bli mer intressanta om förtroendet för amerikansk skuld försvagas.

Kan en besvikelse på AI och ett svagare förtroende för dollarn sammanfalla och skapa en ketchupeffekt för Bitcoin? Vi följer resonemanget, möjligheterna och riskerna bakom scenariot.

item.title: bitcoin ist - Wissen statt FOMO – 24) ... Energie mit zwei Leben
item.description:
Bitcoin und Energieverbrauch werden oft in einem negativen Zusammenhang genannt. Diese Folge zeigt ein differenzierteres Bild: warum Bitcoin-Mining Stromnetze stabilisieren kann, wie aus Abwärme ein zweiter Wertschöpfungskreislauf entsteht, und wo die Grenzen dieser Entwicklung aktuell noch liegen.

Themen in dieser Folge:

item.title: The Café Bitcoin Podcast – The Finale: Liquid's 4,000 Bitcoin, the Caching Bug, and 50 Days for Freedom Wrapped
item.description:
• The last day. Brady opened with the count, 37 shows in 50 days, and the campaign's frame: political independence 250 years ago, monetary independence now. Yan Pritzker, Frank Corva, Suze and Alec on stage; Unseen Finance returned at the end.
  • The Liquid hack, plainly. On Sunday somebody sent 4,000 L-BTC to SideSwap's peg-out and the Liquid Federation paid out real Bitcoin. The L-BTC had been created from nothing. Blockstream paused the sidechain and 3,400 Bitcoin came back Monday.
  • ⭐ Yan on what broke: a caching bug, not anyone's keys. "The only two hard problems in computer science are naming and cache invalidation." Two transactions shared one cache key, so validators mistook a fake for one already checked.
  • Why it is not Bitcoin. Yan: Liquid is an 11-of-15 federation of companies with its own database and rules. "This is a separate thing, this is not Bitcoin itself." Lightning is built on Bitcoin script; Liquid is not.
  • ⭐ Frank on the 15%. The hackers returned 85% and kept about 600 Bitcoin. His question: will anyone be made whole, and if they keep it, "they're surely not white hats." A Bitcoin Policy Institute lawyer offered to talk.
  • Yan's verdict on the hat color: gray. Taking everything to beat a black hat is arguable. Keeping a cut is not. "You don't just return a wallet and take a bunch of stuff out of it."
  • Suze's question: Bitcoiners are ruthless about added trust assumptions, so why did Liquid get a pass? "Were we discerning enough?" Leave the base layer and you take on another code base and another set of failure points.
  • ⭐ Yan on open source in the AI era: it stays because every open project gets red-teamed by the whole internet. Closed systems get hacked too, "we just don't hear about them." The base chain is "the ultimate boss" nobody has beaten.
  • Yan's bank numbers, read live from the Identity Theft Resource Center: 3,332 reported data compromises in 2025 affecting 280 million people, 739 of them in financial services. "Bank-grade security" is not a standard anyone actually meets.
  • ⭐ Frank's hard question: must the layers be as bulletproof as Bitcoin? Yan: nothing is, and the only path is slow growth. Bitcoin was attacked at $1, then $10,000, then a billion. Early adopters carry the risk.
  • Yan's rocket-ship rule. Bitcoin Core engineering is closer to launching a spacecraft than shipping web software. "Years of careful review, study, simulations on other chains." Test new tech on other coins for two years first.
  • Suze asked whether ossification risks losing the skills to change Bitcoin in 50 years. Frank and Yan: no. Ossification is no new features, not no developers, and AI has widened who can work on cryptography and game theory.
  • Yan on open-weight versus hosted AI: the same debate as open source versus closed, and open source won the internet. His advice to companies: externalize memory, skills and harness so you can swap models. Swan built its own.
  • Unseen Finance returned with a proposal: these incidents are a credibility problem for the services on top of Bitcoin, not for Bitcoin. His fix, borrowed from banking: a self-regulatory body plus an insurance pool that service providers pay into.
  • Brady's tally at the close: Cory, Yan, Steve, Alec, Isaiah, Matt and Brandon from Swan; Larry Lepard three times; Parker Lewis, Daniel Batten, Tom and Callum, Guy Swann, Ryan MacLeod, Alana, Bob Burnett, Roxana. Suze made 35 of 37.
  • The close. "We have the tools, we have the knowledge, we have the culture, we have the determination." The half-price buy fee ends today; limit orders placed today keep it. Yan's last word: take security seriously, "go play with AI."

item.title: Swan Signal Live - A Bitcoin Show – John Haar Returns: Why the Fed Must Talk Tough While It Inflates
item.description:
• John reads Warsh's Jackson Hole speech as a nothing burger for Bitcoiners: a Fed chair must talk tough on inflation because signaling anything else would send inflation expectations and yields higher, while the long-run path of financial repression stays the same
  • Warsh reported that 54% of PCE basket components rose more than 3% over the past year, called 4.1% unemployment full employment, and framed inflation as squarely the Fed's problem to solve
  • Markets read the speech as hawkish anyway: the two-year yield rose about 12 basis points while gold and Bitcoin each gave back roughly 3.5%
  • On last week's expanded Treasury buybacks, John points to two signals: a 30-year yield near 5.3% is clearly bothering policymakers, and the Fed has never meaningfully reduced its holdings of 10-year-plus Treasuries even during quantitative tightening, evidence that natural buyers of long-dated government paper are scarce
  • The hosts revisit the shallowest bear market thesis they developed together on this show: a roughly 52% drawdown against 77% to 90%-plus in prior cycles, with the June low of $58,000 sitting just below the 200-week moving average before price rocketed back through it
  • John explains why he believes the June low will hold, while framing the 50-week moving average near $82,000 as the level the market is watching to declare a new bull market
  • Glassnode data shows 1.05 million Bitcoin of long-term holder supply with a cost basis between $83,000 and $86,000, the first heavy resistance shelf above spot, and the hosts discuss how cost basis shapes market psychology
  • The debasement trade is back in ETF volumes, with GLD and IBIT both in the top ten most traded funds, and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio breaking its year-long downtrend after gold's 2025 outperformance
  • Bitcoin's long correlation with software stocks broke down in June, and John argues it was always the wrong frame, a point Lyn Alden's Wall Street Journal essay makes at length: Bitcoin is a protocol of value, not another technology stock
  • A broad Treasury ETF has returned roughly negative 18% after inflation over fifteen years while the supply of government debt keeps expanding, the picture John says is quietly ending the era of Treasuries as the world's default store of value

item.title: The Bitcoin Matrix – Aaron Siri: The One Product You Can't Sue in America
item.description:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

🎙️ GUEST

Aaron Siri — Managing partner of Siri & Glimstad. Lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN). Author of the new book Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines.

item.itunes:summary:
"People say 'I believe in vaccines.' Nobody says that about seatbelts."

Aaron Siri is the managing partner of Siri & Glimstad and, by most measures, the most consequential vaccine litigator in America. He's the attorney behind the famous nine-hour deposition of Dr. Stanley Plotkin — the man they call the godfather of vaccines — lead counsel for the Informed Consent Action Network (ICAN), a 2025 Senate witness, and a central legal figure in the RFK-era reshaping of federal vaccine policy. His new book is Vaccines, Amen: The Religion of Vaccines — in his words, "a cross-examination in book form."

This one steps outside the show's usual lane, and I want to be upfront: this is not medical advice, I'm not a doctor, and everything Aaron argues here is his own case — where it's contested by public-health bodies, treat it as one side of an open debate. What ties it to this show is the question we always ask: how do you know what's real when you're not allowed to check? From there we go deep — how a custody case led to the legendary Plotkin deposition; the Hepatitis B shot Aaron says was licensed on a trial of 147 kids, five days of monitoring, and no control group; the 1986 law he calls "the original sin" that handed vaccine makers liability immunity; the Ford Pinto and what punitive damages actually do; informed consent versus the right to refuse; whether vaccines really stop transmission; and the measles-mortality data he argues almost no one talks about. A conversation about evidence, incentives, and who gets to audit the people in charge.

Subscribe so you never miss an episode.

item.title: No Second Best - A Bitcoin Podcast – Did the Federal Reserve Just Open the Door to Bitcoin?
item.description:
Jamie Dimon just went on national television to push back against Bitcoin and crypto legislation. Hours later, a Bitcoin exchange gained direct access to the Federal Reserve's settlement rails.

At the same time, Morgan Stanley filed for a spot Bitcoin ETF while geopolitical tensions escalated in the Middle East and Bitcoin surged.

This episode breaks down the growing conflict between the traditional banking system and the emerging Bitcoin financial infrastructure, and why the global monetary system may already be bending toward neutral, hard money.

item.title: Der Bitcoin Kompass: Wegweiser im Kaninchenbau – Folge 5: Der Bitcoin-Preis – Zwischen Angebot, Nachfrage und Geldpolitik
item.description:
Was bestimmt eigentlich den Bitcoin-Preis? In Folge 5 vom Bitcoin-Kompass sprechen wir üeber eines der meistdiskutierten Themen im Bitcoin-Space: den Preis. Dabei geht es nicht um Prognosen oder Kaufempfehlungen, sondern um ein grundlegendes Verständnis dafüer, wie der Bitcoin-Preis entsteht und welche Kraefte ihn beeinflussen.


Wir erklären, wie Angebot und Nachfrage auf Bitcoin-Börsen funktionieren, warum das Handelsvolumen oft wichtiger ist als der Preis selbst und welche Rolle die Marktkapitalisierung spielt. Ausserdem beleuchten wir die grossen Einflussfaktoren: das Bitcoin-Halving und den Vier-Jahres-Zyklus, die Geldpolitik der US-Notenbank (Fed), Inflation und die wachsenden Staatsschulden der USA. Im Vergleich zwischen Bitcoin und Gold zeigen sie, warum Bitcoin technologisch ueberlegen sein könnte - und warum der Preis letztlich ein Spiegel des wachsenden Vertrauens in diese neue Technologie ist.


Mehr Infos, interaktive Grafiken zur Marktkapitalisierung und Kontaktmoeglichkeiten findet ihr auf:


Webseite: https://derbitcoinkompass.ch

E-Mail: kontakt@derbitcoinkompass.ch

Telegram: https://t.me/btc_kaninchenbau


Feedback und Fragen gerne per E-Mail, ueber Telegram oder ueber unsere Webseite.

(00:01:31) Volatilitaet und der aktuelle Bitcoin-Preis

(00:02:33) Kaufkraft, Inflation und warum Menschen investieren

(00:05:20) Marktkapitalisierung: Bitcoin vs. Gold vs. Immobilien vs. Aktien

(00:13:26) In was messen wir den Preis? Euro, Dollar oder Aepfel?

(00:17:03) Warum Geld kein stabiler Massstab ist

(00:18:10) Bitcoins festes Angebot: Maximal 21 Millionen

(00:20:02) Das Halving und der Vier-Jahres-Zyklus

(00:24:22) Die Fed, Zinspolitik und US-Staatsschulden

(00:31:27) Was bedeutet das alles fuer den Bitcoin-Preis?

(00:33:37) Bitcoin vs. Gold: Vorteile und Unterschiede

(00:40:30) Preisprognose: Bitcoin auf 1 Million Dollar?

(00:41:54) Zusammenfassung & Verabschiedung

item.title: Store of Bitcoin - Bitcoin as Store of Value – Ep. 49 - Daniel Batten | A new different wave of Bitcoin Adopters.
item.description:
In this episode of Store of Bitcoin, host Alessandro Ottaviani welcomes Daniel Batten, a prominent Bitcoin analyst and investor, to discuss the evolving narrative surrounding Bitcoin, particularly in relation to energy consumption and environmental impact. Daniel shares insights on how the mainstream media's perception of Bitcoin has shifted from skepticism to a more favorable view, largely due to rigorous research and advocacy from the Bitcoin community. He emphasizes the importance of effectively communicating Bitcoin's benefits to various stakeholders, including policymakers and investors, to foster broader adoption.

The conversation delves into the challenges of reaching new adopters, particularly those who may not be motivated by the same values that initially attracted early Bitcoin enthusiasts. Daniel highlights the need for a more nuanced approach to education and outreach, focusing on the social and environmental benefits of Bitcoin. He also discusses the potential for Bitcoin to serve as a tool for financial inclusion in developing countries, where it can provide a safeguard against inflation and empower individuals in oppressive regimes. The episode concludes with a look at future trends in Bitcoin adoption and the importance of aligning messaging with the values of diverse audiences.

item.title: All In Bitcoin – Least Uncertain Money: Joe Burnett on Bitcoin as the Ultimate Store of Value
item.description: Join us as we explore the fascinating world of Bitcoin with Joe Burnett from Unchained. From his journey during the 2017 bull market to helping secure billions in Bitcoin today, Joe offers insights on why Bitcoin stands out as "the least uncertain form of money" and how multi-signature security is changing the game for Bitcoin holders.In this episode, we dive into:Why Bitcoin's fixed monetary policy creates certainty in an uncertain worldHow Unchained secures $10 billion worth of Bitcoin through multi-signature technologyThe concept of "Bitcoin as a hurdle rate" that's changing investment thinkingWhy quantum computing concerns are being addressed by Bitcoin developersPlus: The fundamental difference between owning actual Bitcoin versus IOUs from exchangesKey timestamps:00:00:55 - Joe's reaction to Bitcoin hitting 100K versus previous milestones00:03:21 - Defining Bitcoin maximalism and money's core purpose00:05:46 - Why Bitcoin has the least future uncertainty of any money00:08:23 - The dollar's role today and Bitcoin's future as everyday money00:12:48 - Joe's Bitcoin origin story and early misconceptions00:17:13 - How the bear market helped Joe discover Bitcoin's true value00:20:12 - Unchained's custody product and how it protects $10 billion in Bitcoin00:22:39 - How multi-signature security works and eliminates single points of failure00:27:11 - The range of Bitcoin products Unchained offers beyond basic custody00:30:38 - Bitcoin as a hurdle rate: A new way to think about investments00:33:53 - Quantum computing and Bitcoin's adaptability to future threats00:37:23 - Final thoughts: Getting started with Bitcoin and maintaining a long-term horizonWhether you're new to Bitcoin or a seasoned HODLer, this episode offers valuable perspectives on Bitcoin as the superior form of money, practical security considerations, and forward-thinking concepts that may shape how we view investments in the coming years.

item.title: Crypto4Bitcoin – What is Xircus ???
item.description: Xircus (XW3) is a cryptocurrency associated with the Xircus Web3 protocol, which is positioned to become a go-to platform for Web3. Xircus is building the infrastructure layer structure for building and scaling Web3 businesses and brands with its no-code reduces costs and achieves a faster time-to-market. The protocol has achieved a remarkable feat by building a fully functional no-code and low-code Web3 despite the challenging market conditions. It has also announced a seed investment round and is offering investors a unique opportunity to participate in a seed sale. Xircus has designed its user- and developer-friendly platform to streamline the DApp building process, making it quicker, easier, and more cost-effective. The platform's unique XircusSkins and XircusModules protocol allows designers and developers to monetize their skills, while DApp owners can choose from a range of niche-specific skins and modules that are both upgradeable and scalable. Xircus is on a mission to transform the current landscape, offering a dynamic platform that caters to Web3 enthusiasts, developers, and entrepreneurs

item.title: De Cero a Bitcoin – #23 ¿Hiperbitcoinización en Argentina de la mano de Javier Milei?
item.description:
Con la llegada del primer presidente liberal libertario a la Argentina se abren miles de interrogantes, pero hay uno que quisiera tratar el día de hoy. ¿Es posible en este contexto una hiperbitcoinización en Argentina? Bueno la primera respuesta nos la ha dado la canciller Diana Mondino quien en estos días ha twitteado lo siguiente: “Ratificamos y confirmamos que en Argentina se podrán pactar contratos en Bitcoin”. Pero no me podía quedar solamente con esto, tenía que buscar más información y por eso acudí a alguien que habló con el actual presidente sobre Bitcoin, no solo eso sino que fue uno de los fundadores del partido liberal libertario. El es Ariel Aguilar, más conocido en redes como Evangelista Bitcoin, con quien repasaré el pasado, el presente y el futuro de Argentina y Bitcoin. Una aclaración importante, el capítulo fue grabado previo a la asunción del presidente.

Espero que lo disfruten, un episodio muy Bullish.

item.title: Meet the Bitcoin Taco Plebs - Bitcoin Magazine – Building Access To Bitcoin For Everyone w/ SeedSigner
item.description:
To be frank, I didn’t expect this podcast to be so profound! 

When I invited SeedSigner on to talk about his project, I was hoping to discuss all the cool technical aspects, his ideas for the future and Bitcoin 2022. While we touched on all of these awesome things, what I found really compelling in our conversation was the guiding principles of the project SeedSigner highlighted. 

Having access to Bitcoin, an open monetary network that does not debase your wealth, is a human right. Many countries or jurisdictions may stifle the bitcoin industry, making it impossible for some people to acquire hardware wallets that are otherwise common in the world. This project is an example of open-source software and engineering coming together to provide ever increasing access to Bitcoin. 

SeedSigner highlighted the importance of providing access to custody solutions that prioritize the DIY, verifiable and transparent aspects of hardware and software. While he did say that the project could potentially some day have a second form that would increase scalability and minimize self assembly, there are no solid plans for this now, as their full attention remains on the DIY side of things. 

One thing that stuck out to me from the conversation was his highlighting of the importance of fungibility and privacy. The two go hand in hand — if certain UTXOs are being labeled as criminal, those UTXOs must be subject to scrutiny that would deem them so. We also discussed if he thought CoinJoin and other similar privacy implementations are the key to this.

Of course, I can’t help but ask our current guests about Bitcoin 2022 — especially considering SeedSigner will be speaking there! If you haven’t already, please check out his article on his experience at Bitcoin 2021. In it, he details how it was his first real Bitcoin gathering, introducing his project and more.

At Bitcoin 2022, SeedSigner expressed his desire to continue to discuss his project with other people, but also, to finally catch up on all the other projects and happenings in the industry that seem to be flying by. I can fully relate to this feeling. 

Make sure to check out the entire podcast and follow SeedSigner on Twitter for more updates on this project. And of course, I hope to see you all in Miami!
